blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: A model behind an API can be identified from its one-word answers to everyday questions such as "Name a sound" or "Name a poet". A model's profile records how often it gives each answer to each question. We attribute new answers to the model most likely to have given them. On a panel of 94 models, 40 answers identify the exact model 92.5% of the time, against 1.1% by chance. Profiles built through OpenRouter identified all ten models served by DeepInfra under blinded labels. A system prompt lowers accuracy by 6 to 16 points. We applied the method to 96 endpoints of 13 open models on OpenRouter, and 92 identify as the model they claim. Of the other four, one matches the claimed model with reasoning turned off. One serves Gemma 4 under the name Llama 4 Maverick: it names itself Gemma 4, and it is billed Gemma 4's token counts on every message. Two remain unresolved. Billing records also show context added to first-party models. Grok 4.7 is billed 1,247 input tokens for a one-line question that costs GPT-4o only 12 tokens, and five models state the current date without being billed for it. The questions come from a public census of model defaults, and the method costs cents per endpoint.
blocks.zh: API背后的模型可以从其对日常问题的单词解答中识别出来,如"一个声音的名字"或"一个诗人的名字". 一个模型的剖面记录了它给每个问题每个答案的频率. 我们把新答案归结到最有可能给出的模型上. 在94个模型的小组中,40个答案确定了时间的92.5%的准确模型,而1.1%。 通过OpenRouter构建的配置文件确定了DeepInfra在被蒙蔽的标签下服务的所有十个模型. 一个系统提示将精度降低6至16分. 我们在OpenRouter上的13个开放型号的96个端点上应用了这种方法,92个确定为他们声称的型号. 在另外四个人中,有一个符合声称的模型 推理关闭。 一个是用Llama 4 Maverick这个名字为Gemma 4服务:它自己是Gemma 4, 它被记上Gemma 4每条消息的代币。 有两项尚未解决。 计费记录还显示在第一党模式中添加的内容. Grok 4.7为单行问题开具了1,247个输入符,只花费了GPT-4o的12个令牌,有5个型号说明当前日期而没有为此开具账单. 这些问题来自对模型默认的公开普查,以及方法成本每端点.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
A deployed language model is usually a name behind an API. The caller sees neither the weights
nor how they are served. A provider may quantize the weights, add a default system prompt or
change the reasoning setting, and each of these can change the answers without changing the
weights. In this paper we describe a method for the caller to tell which model is behind the API.

改变推理设置,每个都可以改变答案而不改变
重量。 在本文中,我们描述了一个调用者告诉API背后是哪个模型的方法.

blocks.en:
Recent work shows that short, constrained answers can identify a model. IRIS attributes endpoints
from requests for random digits and bit strings, with a trained classifier [ 14 ] . Bruckner [1] verifies model identity from single-token answers to tasks such as
“name a random number”. FLIPS identifies configured instances from requested random binary
sequences [ 12 ] .

从随机数字和比特字符串的请求中,带有训练有素的分类器 [14] 。 布鲁克纳 [1] 从单键答案验证模型身份到诸如任务
“点一个随机数字”。 FLIPS 从请求的随机二进制中识别已配置实例
序列 [12].

blocks.en:
A census of model defaults asked 105 models 96 one-word questions such as “Name a color” and
“Name a fruit”, repeated eight times per question [ 10 ] . Models converge
strongly on these questions, as they do on open-ended prompts [ 8 ] . The
answers that depart from the consensus repeat within a model. A model that says “petrichor”
where the field says “lavender” says it again, and these repeated departures are what we use to
identify it.

the auditor’s message, and § 5 shows that this happens.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
IRIS [ 14 ] is the closest prior work. It sends
short random-generation requests (a coin draw, a digit, an integer in a range, a bit or digit
sequence) and classifies the responses with a random forest over 179 string features. On 17
OpenRouter endpoints it reaches 0.965 attribution accuracy at 8 queries. On 45 models it reaches
0.90 at 16 queries. It also flags 14 of 15 same-model OpenRouter provider pairs as
distinguishable. IRIS reports that a generic text classifier cannot attribute providers from
natural-language completions. Our answers are natural language, but each is one word to a fixed
question, so they can be counted.

短随机生成请求( 硬币图纸、 数字、 范围整数、 位数或位数)

自然语言的完成。 我们的答案是自然语言, 但是每个词都是一个字到固定的
问,所以可以计算。

blocks.en:
Bruckner [1] samples 165 OpenRouter models
on ten one-token tasks in four languages. Jensen–Shannon distance between answer distributions
gives verification at a 7.3% equal error rate with the full 40-cell battery, and family
assignment at 59.5%. Bruckner reports no closed-set identification of the exact model. FLIPS [ 12 ] uses biases in requested binary sequences. It treats a model under a
different system prompt or quantization as a different instance. It reports 96% closed-set and
90% open-set identification over 237 instances.

不同的系统即时或量化为不同的实例。 它报告96%的封闭集和
在237个案例中,90%的开放式身份确认。

blocks.en:
LLMmap [ 11 ] identifies 42 model
versions at over 95% from eight crafted queries with a trained model. Chen et al. [3] show that a one-sentence tone prefix in the system prompt drops clone detection on short
structured outputs from 0.978 to 0.547.

结构化产出从0.978降至0.547。

blocks.en:
Model Equality Testing [ 6 ] tests whether an API serves a
reference distribution with an MMD two-sample test, and finds 11 of 31 Llama endpoints serving
different distributions from Meta’s weights. The rank-based uniformity test [ 16 ] detects quantization, fine-tuning and swaps from outputs. Cai et al. [2] argue that
software-only checks are unreliable and propose trusted execution. Stability Monitor [ 9 ] detects changes in version, stack and quantization from output
distributions and finds stability differences across hosts of one model. AgentProv [ 13 ] is the source of our check in § 5.3 . Its token-count scan
finds 44% of 75 OpenRouter open-weight endpoints off the official chat template, some with
injected system prompts. Under an injected prompt, MET and RUT falsely reject honest models 67%
and 53% of the time.

blocks.en:
We compared the likelihood with two simpler scorers on the
same folds and question draws. One picks the model whose answers are closest in Jensen–Shannon
distance, as in Bruckner [1] . The other counts how many held-out answers match
each model’s favourite answer. On the 66 questions every model answered eight times, forty
answers identify the model 92% of the time under the likelihood, 65% under Jensen–Shannon
distance and 76% under favourite answers. The likelihood scores best at every budget
(Appendix E ). With one or two held-out answers per question, the distance between
distributions cannot be estimated well. Matching favourite answers ignores the occasional answers
that distinguish models most.

Greedy selection adds, one at a time, the question that most raises the probability given to the
true model. To keep selection apart from scoring, questions are chosen on half of each model’s
samples and scored on the other half. The halves are then swapped, and Table 2 averages the two. Selected and random sets both come from the 66 questions every model answered
eight times.

样品和得分的另一半。 然后将两半交替,表2平均为两者. 选集和随机集都来自每个模型回答的66个问题

Selection beats random sets at every size, by 14 points at ten questions. The questions it picks

Selection is tuned to this panel, so its advantage on unseen models is likely smaller.

Ten panel models were queried through DeepInfra under random code names, two samples per question:

blocks.en:
Writer markets Palmyra X5 as its own model and has not named a base model for it. Writer’s report
on the successor, Palmyra x6, names GLM-5.2 as that model’s base [ 4 ] . Palmyra
X5’s nearest model on our 96 questions is Qwen3 235B Instruct (2507), by 2.3 nats per question over
the next candidate. Qwen3 235B’s nearest model is Palmyra X5. Bruckner [1] found the
same pair at a distance equal to the median distance between halves of one model. Mutual nearest
neighbours show that the two answer alike. They do not prove that one is derived from the other.

context may shape its answers.

blocks.en: 5.1 Setup

blocks.en:
OpenRouter routes each open model to one of several providers, with declared precision (bf16,
fp8, fp4, int4 or unstated) and prices that differ up to thirtyfold for one model. We pinned each
of 104 endpoints of 14 open models in turn, with fallbacks off, and asked all 96 questions four
times. Eight could not be scored. Four returned no data, and four claim Qwen3.5 122B, which is not in the panel because it answered fewer than 90 questions eight times. The rest of this
section reports the other 96 endpoints, of 13 models. The whole audit cost $7.20 over 36,918
calls. The released transcripts identify each endpoint by provider. The text characterizes
endpoints and names no third-party provider; Appendix G lists them by model and
letter.

Each endpoint is scored two ways. Identification ranks the 94 panel profiles by the likelihood of

endpoint with the pooled answers of the same model’s other providers, collected the same day. The
distance is the mean Jensen–Shannon divergence across questions. Its p p -value comes from 1,000
label permutations within each question, with Benjamini–Hochberg correction across endpoints.

blocks.en:
An endpoint can serve the claimed weights and still answer differently, because text was added
before the auditor’s message. AgentProv shows that this makes equality tests reject honest models.
Section 4.4 shows it lowers identification accuracy. A provider pays to process
added text on every call, so billed input tokens above the count for the sent message reveal it.

model told nothing can only guess the date. GPT-5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 mini and GPT-5.5 stated the
correct date in both samples. Each was billed 11 input tokens for the question. GPT-5.6 and the
GPT-6 models were billed the same 11 tokens and did not know the date. Muse Spark 1.3, from
another lab, also stated the date in both samples while billed 12 tokens. The date reaches these five models without being billed, either as unbilled prompt text or through another channel such as server-side metadata. Either way, billed tokens are a
lower bound on added context.

blocks.en: 6 Limitations
blocks.zh: 6. 限制

blocks.en:
1. Serving nondeterminism. Outputs from one endpoint vary with load, batch size and
hardware [ 7 ] . Byte-identical next-day replays agree at 0.78 in a
preregistered study of shared endpoints [ 15 ] . Nondeterminism moves token
probabilities most in the range 0.1 to 0.9 [ 5 ] , which is where contested
answers lie. Our stability measure in § 4.5 is coarse: it checks only each model’s
favourite answer. 2. Closed set. The method picks among profiled models. An unseen model is assigned to
its nearest relative. Open-set rejection is untested. 3. Added context and routing. Some first-party models and some providers receive text
before the caller’s message (§ 5.3 ). Our profiles were built through OpenRouter’s
default routing, so they include whatever was added there. A profile describes a model as served.
It also mixes providers. On the audit day four of ten unpinned calls to Llama 4 Maverick were
billed the token counts of the endpoint serving Gemma 4, but the Maverick profile was collected in July and September and
holds about 0.5% Gemma 4 answers. The Mistral Small 3.2 profile is about 17% from the developer’s
own endpoint (§ 5.2 ). Pinned reference profiles leave the audit’s conclusions
unchanged, but the identification results in § 4 rest on mixed profiles. 4. Billing is a lower bound. Five models received the date with no billed tokens
(§ 5.3 ). Context that is not billed cannot be found by the billed-token check. 5. Within-family confusion. Most errors at small budgets fall outside the true family.
As answers grow, the remaining errors move inside it, and at 96 questions all of them are within
one family. 6. Reasoning setting. Profiles were built at each model’s default reasoning setting. A
hybrid model served with reasoning off can resemble a different model, as Kimi K2.5 resembles
Kimi K2 (§ 5.4 ). Profiling hybrid models in both settings would close this gap. 7. Temperature. All data are at temperature 1. 8. No matched baseline from prior work. We did not run random-sequence probes on this
panel, so any comparison with IRIS and FLIPS rests on their published numbers. 9. Gaming. A provider who knows the public questions could route them to the genuine
model, add an answer key in a hidden prompt, or fine-tune a cheaper model to imitate the answers.
A rotating secret reserve of questions could mitigate the first. The billed-token check could
catch the second only when the added text is billed (limitation 4). None of this is tested. Many
questions carry similar information (§ 4.2 ), so a reserve of new questions may work as
well as the published ones. Random sets of 40 questions already identify the model 89% to 94% of
the time, whichever 40 are drawn (Appendix E ).

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
One-word answers to everyday questions identify the model behind an API. Forty answers pick one of
94 models 92.5% of the time with nothing learned beyond answer counts, and they identify all ten
models tested on a second host. Each decision can be checked by reading the answers behind it. Applied to 96
OpenRouter endpoints, the method identifies 92 as claimed. One of the four exceptions matches the
claimed model served with reasoning off. Another is Gemma 4 served under the name Llama 4 Maverick.
The other two remain unresolved. Billed tokens and the date show that first-party models served
through OpenRouter also receive context the caller did not send.

94个型号 时间的92.5% 没有学到什么 答案计数之外,
模型在第二个主机上测试. 每个决定可以通过阅读其背后的答案来检查. 适用于96年
OpenRouter 端点,该方法确定92为所称. 四个例外之一与
声称的模型提供了推理。 另一个是Gemma 4,用名字Llama 4 Maverick服务。
其他两个问题仍未解决。 记账牌和日期显示第一党模型服务
通过 OpenRouter 也可以收到调用者没有发送的上下文 。

blocks.en: Appendix C From reply to answer
blocks.zh: 附录C

blocks.en:
Replies are reduced to answers in six steps ( analyze.py ). 1. Strip a closed reasoning block, chat-template tokens, a leading “ASSISTANT:”, anything
after a stop marker, and leftover tags. Reasoning returned in the API’s separate reasoning field is
never read. 2. Take the first line that is an answer, skipping lead-ins (“Sure, here is one:”) and
asides. A self-correction (“Wait, … One word: Stonehenge”) replaces the first answer. 3. Lower-case, fold accents, drop punctuation and emoji, and take the last word, so “A common
color is blue.” gives “blue”. A two- or three-word name ending in a generic head noun of its
category is joined (“soy sauce” to “soysauce”, “golden retriever” to “goldenretriever”). 4. Drop failed cells: unclosed reasoning, a reply that opens as leaked reasoning, replies over
15 words, bare acknowledgments, single letters and function words. They are not scored. Of 72,192
panel cells, 83 (0.11%) give no usable answer; the most are Mixtral 8x22B (23) and Mistral Small
2603 (19). 5. Merge spelling variants with a hand-checked map per category, built from a similarity scan
and a category-by-category review by four reviewers before any fingerprint analysis. Near-matches
that are different things are kept apart (serenity and serendipity, pine and pineapple). 6. Merge plurals: an answer ending in “s” becomes its stem when the stem occurs in the panel’s
answers to that question. Answers from outside the panel (the blind test, the audit, the follow-ups) go through the same
steps and are merged onto the panel’s answers.
